merger_name: Regis – Home Care Business of Royal Freemasons
merger_description:
Regis Aged Care Pty Ltd (**Regis**) proposes to acquire the Royal Freemasons Home Care business from Royal Freemasons Ltd (**Royal Freemasons**) (the **Acquisition**). This includes associated client relationships, operational assets, and other business assets necessary for the ongoing provision of home care services. The transaction does not involve the acquisition of Royal Freemasons’ residential aged care, retirement living, or other aged care operations.

Regis is an ASX-listed Australian aged care provider operating residential aged care homes, home care services, and retirement living services across Australia. Its home care operations provide government-funded and privately funded in-home care and support services to older Australians, including personal care, domestic assistance, nursing and allied health support, social support, and care management services.

Royal Freemasons is a not-for-profit aged care and retirement living provider operating primarily in Victoria. Through its Royal Freemasons Home Care business, it supplies home care services to older Australians, including personal care, domestic assistance, nursing support, respite services, social support, and care management services.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition given:
a. the parties’ combined share of supply of in-home aged
care and support services in Victoria (primarily in Greater
Melbourne) is low and the increment arising from the
Acquisition would be small
b. there are alternative providers of in-home aged care and
support services in Greater Melbourne and in Victoria more
broadly.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
